judged_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed object keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()], which evaluate to literal property names "z.string().toString()" / "z.string().optional().toString()", so the schema requires a number-valued property literally named "z.string().toString()". With APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, safeParse(response) fails for every real token payload (no provider returns such a key), so parseRefreshTokenResponse throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" and the refresh is aborted for Google, Office365, Zoom, and Salesforce — the credential-sync feature this PR adds cannot work at all, and callers like GoogleCalendarService never reach the credential update.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. In a JS object literal those computed keys evaluate immediately to a single literal string key (whatever `toString()` returns for the Zod object), not a “match any string key” index signature. That means the schema requires a number-valued property with that literal key, so `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` will fail for normal OAuth token payloads. Since `parseRefreshTokenResponse` selects this schema when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, it will throw `"Invalid refreshed tokens were returned"`, breaking the refresh paths updated to call it (e.g., Google/Office365/Zoom/Salesforce).
